bank.name: Muslim Civilization & Contributions
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: The golden age of Islam — science, culture, architecture and world contributions.

questions.prompt: Who is called the 'Father of Modern Medicine' in the Islamic tradition?
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) wrote the Canon of Medicine (Al-Qanun), a standard medical textbook in Europe for centuries.

questions.prompt: Who discovered the smallpox disease and wrote 'Al-Hawi', the largest medical encyclopedia of the age?
questions.explanation: Al-Razi (865-925 CE) gave the first clinical description of smallpox and measles and wrote Al-Hawi.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with first describing the pulmonary circulation of blood?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Nafis (1213-1288) described pulmonary circulation centuries before William Harvey.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the 'Father of Surgery' for his surgical encyclopedia 'Al-Tasrif'?
questions.explanation: Al-Zahrawi (936-1013) wrote Al-Tasrif, a 30-volume medical work with surgical innovations.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'Al-Qanun fil-Tibb' (The Canon of Medicine)?
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina's Al-Qanun fil-Tibb was the standard medical text in European universities until the 17th century.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Algebra'?
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi wrote 'Al-Jabr wal-Muqabala', from which the word 'algebra' and 'algorithm' derive.

questions.prompt: Who is called the 'Father of Optics' for his 'Book of Optics' (Kitab al-Manazir)?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham (965-1040) pioneered the scientific method and correct theory of vision in Kitab al-Manazir.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the 'Shahnameh' (Book of Kings), the Persian epic?
questions.explanation: Ferdowsi composed the Shahnameh, Iran's national epic, completed around 1010 CE.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the 'Rubaiyat' (quatrains) and also reformed the Persian calendar?
questions.explanation: Omar Khayyam, mathematician and poet, devised a solar calendar more accurate than the Gregorian.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the 'Second Teacher' (after Aristotle) for his contributions to philosophy and logic?
questions.explanation: Al-Farabi (872-950) is called 'Muallim-e-Sani' (the Second Teacher) after Aristotle.

questions.prompt: Who is called the 'Philosopher of Islam' and wrote commentaries on Aristotle known as 'The Commentator'?
questions.explanation: Ibn Rushd (1126-1198) was known in Europe as 'The Commentator' for his commentaries on Aristotle.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim geographer calculated the circumference of the Earth with remarkable accuracy?
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni (973-1048) calculated the Earth's circumference and radius with great precision.

questions.prompt: Who drew the 'Tabula Rogeriana', one of the most advanced medieval world maps?
questions.explanation: Al-Idrisi created the Tabula Rogeriana for King Roger II of Sicily in 1154.

questions.prompt: Which famous traveler visited China, India and West Africa, covering about 120,000 km?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta (1304-1369) traveled across the Islamic world and beyond, writing the Rihla.

questions.prompt: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Sociology' for his 'Muqaddimah'?
questions.explanation: Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah (1377) laid the foundations of sociology and historiography.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim chemist is credited with the discovery of sulfuric acid and distillation techniques?
questions.explanation: Jabir ibn Hayyan (8th century) is called the 'Father of Chemistry' for his experiments and discoveries.

questions.prompt: Which magnificent structure in India was built by the Muslim Mughal emperor Shah Jahan?
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra (1632-1653) in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Muslim ruler to conquer Sindh in 712 CE?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim, an Umayyad general, conquered Sindh in 712 CE.

questions.prompt: The first university in the world, Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, was founded by whom?
questions.explanation: Fatima al-Fihri founded Al-Qarawiyyin in 859 CE, recognized by UNESCO as the oldest university.

questions.prompt: Which Abbasid caliph established the 'Bayt al-Hikmah' (House of Wisdom) in Baghdad?
questions.explanation: Caliph Al-Mamun (r. 813-833) established the House of Wisdom, the intellectual hub of the Golden Age.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic city was the world's largest during the 10th century?
questions.explanation: Cordoba in Al-Andalus became one of the largest and most advanced cities of its age.

questions.prompt: The 'Al-Zahrawi' contributions were mainly in which field?
questions.explanation: Al-Zahrawi (Abulcasis) is the father of modern surgery, with 200+ instruments.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scholar is called the 'Philosopher of the Arabs' (Failasuf al-Arab)?
questions.explanation: Al-Kindi (801-873) was the first great Muslim philosopher.

questions.prompt: The decimal number system (including zero) reached Europe through which Muslim works?
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi's 'On the Calculation with Hindu Numerals' spread the decimal system.

questions.prompt: The first systematic hospital (Bimaristan) in the Islamic world was established in?
questions.explanation: The Bimaristan of Baghdad, under Harun al-Rashid, was a pioneer hospital.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim engineer built elaborate water clocks and automata, described in 'Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices'?
questions.explanation: Al-Jazari (1136-1206) is the father of robotics and modern engineering.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim astronomer calculated the solar year accurately and built observatories at Maragha?
questions.explanation: Nasir al-Din al-Tusi (1201-1274) directed the Maragha observatory.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim traveler wrote the 'Rihla', describing his journeys across 40+ countries?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta's Rihla documents 29 years of travel across the Islamic world and beyond.

questions.prompt: The Islamic art of 'Arabesque' and geometric patterns is characterized by?
options: Repeating geometric and floral patterns without human figures
questions.explanation: Arabesque and geometric design reflect Tawheed through non-figurative art.

questions.prompt: Which Mamluk sultan built a famous hospital complex in Cairo in 1285?
questions.explanation: The Qalawun complex in Cairo included a hospital, mausoleum and madrasa.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scholar founded the observatory and library known as 'Bayt al-Hikmah'?
questions.explanation: Al-Mamun expanded Bayt al-Hikmah with an observatory and translation bureau.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic invention improved navigation and was adopted worldwide?
questions.explanation: Muslims refined the astrolabe for navigation and astronomy; its use spread globally.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim geographer's map 'Tabula Rogeriana' served Europeans for three centuries?
questions.explanation: Al-Idrisi's 1154 map for King Roger II was among the most accurate of its time.

questions.prompt: Which field did Al-Kindi pioneer in cryptography?
questions.explanation: Al-Kindi's 'Manuscript on Deciphering Cryptographic Messages' introduced frequency analysis.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim polymath discovered the camera obscura principle?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham's optical experiments demonstrated the camera obscura.

questions.prompt: The first flying machine concept was sketched by which Muslim inventor?
questions.explanation: Abbas ibn Firnas (9th century, Cordoba) made a gliding flight attempt.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic institution preserved Greek philosophy, later transmitted to Europe?
options: Bayt al-Hikmah and the translation movement
questions.explanation: The translation movement in Baghdad preserved and advanced Greek knowledge.

questions.prompt: Which city hosted the world's first public library with a lending system?
options: Baghdad and Cordoba both pioneered libraries
questions.explanation: Abbasid Baghdad and Umayyad Cordoba hosted magnificent public libraries.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scientist laid foundations of trigonometry with the sine function?
questions.explanation: Al-Battani (850-929) made major advances in trigonometry and astronomy.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the famous medical canon 'Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb'?
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina authored the Canon of Medicine.

questions.prompt: Who is known as the father of optics?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham pioneered the science of optics.

questions.prompt: Al-Zahrawi is famous as the father of:
questions.explanation: Al-Zahrawi is the father of modern surgery.

questions.prompt: The scholar Al-Biruni wrote a famous book on:
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni's Kitab-ul-Hind studied Indian culture.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scholar is known as the 'father of chemistry'?
questions.explanation: Jabir ibn Hayyan is the father of chemistry.

questions.prompt: The philosopher Ibn Rushd is known in Europe as:
questions.explanation: Ibn Rushd was called Averroes in the West.

questions.prompt: The Islamic university Al-Qarawiyyin is located in:
questions.explanation: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez is among the world's oldest universities.

questions.prompt: The Great Mosque of Cordoba is a masterpiece of:
questions.explanation: Cordoba's mosque reflects Andalusian Umayyad architecture.

questions.prompt: The Alhambra palace is located in:
questions.explanation: The Alhambra stands in Granada.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim explorer is famous for his travels from Tangier?
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta travelled across the medieval world.

questions.prompt: The cartographer Al-Idrisi created maps for which ruler?
questions.explanation: Al-Idrisi made the Tabula Rogeriana for Roger II.

questions.prompt: The 'Zubaidah' canal in Iraq was built during which caliphate?
questions.explanation: Zubaidah, Harun al-Rashid's wife, funded the canal.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic city was known as the 'Jewel of the World'?
questions.explanation: Cordoba was famed as the jewel of the world.

questions.prompt: The astrolabe was perfected by which Muslim scientist?
questions.explanation: Muslim astronomers like Al-Battani refined the astrolabe.

questions.prompt: The first hospital (Bimaristan) in Islamic history was built in:
questions.explanation: The first Bimaristan was established in Damascus.

questions.prompt: The scholar Al-Ghazali wrote which famous work?
questions.explanation: Al-Ghazali's Ihya revived Islamic spirituality.

questions.prompt: Muslim merchants helped spread Islam to which region in the 13th–15th centuries?
questions.explanation: Traders carried Islam to Southeast Asia.

questions.prompt: The 'Ottoman' miniature and tile art flourished in which city?
questions.explanation: Iznik produced famed Ottoman tiles.

questions.prompt: The famous book 'Kitab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala' was written by whom?
questions.explanation: Al-Khwarizmi's Kitab al-Jabr wal-Muqabala founded algebra.

questions.prompt: The English word 'algebra' is derived from which Arabic term?
questions.explanation: Algebra comes from 'al-Jabr' in Al-Khwarizmi's title.

questions.prompt: The English word 'algorithm' derives from the name of which scholar?
questions.explanation: Algorithm comes from the Latinized form of Al-Khwarizmi's name.

questions.prompt: Ibn Sina is also known in Europe as?
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina (Avicenna) is known as the prince of physicians.

questions.prompt: The English word 'chemistry' is derived from the Arabic?
questions.explanation: Chemistry derives from al-kimiya, the Arabic term for the transmutation art.

questions.prompt: The encyclopedic 'Kitab al-Shifa' (Book of Healing) was written by whom?
questions.explanation: Ibn Sina's Kitab al-Shifa is a vast encyclopedia of philosophy and science.

questions.prompt: Which European city hosted the 12th-century school of translators of Arabic works?
questions.explanation: Toledo's translation school transmitted Arabic science to Europe.

questions.prompt: The Muslim astronomer Al-Battani is famous for accurately determining?
options: The length of the solar year
questions.explanation: Al-Battani measured the tropical year with great precision.

questions.prompt: The 'Muqaddimah' of Ibn Khaldun is a pioneering work on?
options: The rise and fall of civilizations and historiography
questions.explanation: The Muqaddimah analyses the factors behind the rise and decline of states.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'Tahafut al-Falasifah' (The Incoherence of the Philosophers)?
questions.explanation: Al-Ghazali's Tahafut challenged the philosophers of his time.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'Tahafut al-Tahafut' (The Incoherence of the Incoherence)?
questions.explanation: Ibn Rushd replied to Al-Ghazali with Tahafut al-Tahafut.

questions.prompt: The medical encyclopedia 'Kitab al-Mansuri' was written by whom?
questions.explanation: Al-Razi dedicated Kitab al-Mansuri to the Samanid ruler Mansur.

questions.prompt: Al-Zahrawi's 'Al-Tasrif' is famous for containing?
options: The first map of the world
questions.explanation: Al-Tasrif included drawings of over two hundred surgical instruments.

questions.prompt: The word 'alcohol' is derived from the Arabic?
questions.explanation: Alcohol traces to al-kuhl, the fine antimony powder used as eyeliner.

questions.prompt: The word 'zenith' comes from the Arabic word meaning?
questions.explanation: Zenith derives from 'samt al-ra's', the path over one's head.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scholar demonstrated that light travels in straight lines?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham's experiments established rectilinear propagation of light.

questions.prompt: The first Islamic observatory was built by which Abbasid caliph?
questions.explanation: Al-Mamun founded the Shammasiyyah observatory in Baghdad.

questions.prompt: The palace of Madinat al-Zahra near Cordoba was built by whom?
questions.explanation: Abd al-Rahman III built the lavish city-palace of Madinat al-Zahra.

questions.prompt: The Giralda tower in Seville was built by which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Almohads built the Giralda as the minaret of Seville's mosque.

questions.prompt: The Taj Mahal was designed by which architect?
questions.explanation: The Persian architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori is credited with the Taj Mahal's design.

questions.prompt: Al-Farabi's famous work on music is called?
questions.explanation: Al-Farabi's 'Great Book of Music' is a classic of music theory.

questions.prompt: Who wrote 'The Opinions of the People of the Virtuous City'?
questions.explanation: Al-Farabi's virtuous-city treatise outlines his political philosophy.

questions.prompt: Which Andalusian scholar wrote on agriculture in 'Kitab al-Filaha'?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Awwam's Kitab al-Filaha is a famous treatise on agriculture.

questions.prompt: After the Reconquista, the Great Mosque of Cordoba was?
questions.explanation: The mosque-cathedral of Cordoba was converted after the Christian conquest.

questions.prompt: The Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan designed which famous mosque?
questions.explanation: Sinan's Suleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul is his masterpiece.

questions.prompt: The Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed) in Istanbul was designed by whom?
questions.explanation: Sedefkar Mehmed Agha, a student of Sinan, designed the Blue Mosque.

questions.prompt: Which art form did Islamic civilization elevate above figurative painting?
questions.explanation: Islamic calligraphy became the supreme art of the Muslim world.

questions.prompt: Al-Razi was known in Europe as?
questions.explanation: Al-Razi (Rhazes) was one of the greatest clinicians of the age.

questions.prompt: Ibn Rushd wrote which work defending the compatibility of religion and philosophy?
questions.explanation: Fasl al-Maqal argues that philosophy and revelation agree.

questions.prompt: Al-Ghazali's autobiography is called?
questions.explanation: Al-Munqidh min al-Dalal recounts Al-Ghazali's spiritual journey.

questions.prompt: Which city's scholars created the first 'Madrasah' system for higher learning?
questions.explanation: The Nizamiyyah madrasahs of the Seljuk era formalized higher education.

questions.prompt: The 'Nizamiyyah' colleges were founded by which vizier?
questions.explanation: The Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk founded the Nizamiyyah colleges.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim scholar wrote 'The Book of Fixed Stars' (Kitab Suwar al-Kawakib)?
questions.explanation: Al-Sufi's star atlas influenced later astronomy in East and West.

questions.prompt: The Muslim invention of the 'mechanical clock' is credited to which engineer?
questions.explanation: Al-Jazari's water clocks and automata are among the earliest programmable machines.

questions.prompt: The 'elephant clock' described by Al-Jazari was built in which region?
questions.explanation: Al-Jazari worked in Diyarbakir in Upper Mesopotamia (the Jazira).

questions.prompt: Which Muslim chemist developed distillation and discovered nitric acid?
questions.explanation: Jabir ibn Hayyan pioneered distillation and mineral acids.

questions.prompt: Which female scholar established Al-Qarawiyyin as a full university?
questions.explanation: Fatima al-Fihri founded the Qarawiyyin mosque-university in Fez.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic city was described as having 'seventy libraries' and 500,000 books?
questions.explanation: Cordoba in the 10th century boasted immense libraries.

questions.prompt: Which scholar is known as the 'Ptolemy of the Arabs'?
questions.explanation: Al-Battani's astronomical tables earned him this title.

questions.prompt: The 'camera obscura' was described and studied by whom?
questions.explanation: Ibn al-Haytham explained the camera obscura and image formation.

questions.prompt: Which scholar calculated the height of the atmosphere? no
questions.explanation: A placeholder distractor; the correct answer is not Al-Biruni here.

questions.prompt: The word 'nadir' derives from the Arabic 'nazir', meaning?
questions.explanation: Nadir is the point directly opposite the zenith, from Arabic nazir.

questions.prompt: Which Muslim surgeon is considered the father of plastic surgery?
questions.explanation: Al-Zahrawi pioneered reconstructive and plastic surgical techniques.
